items.summary: The strongest purpose-fit signals are microsoft/markitdown for document-to-content extraction, shadcn-ui/ui for accessible reusable UI, and mermaid-js/mermaid for structured explanatory content. Evidence is limited to public repo metadata and disposable-lab review: MarkItDown and shadcn passed bounded checks; Mermaid had no safe native checks without dependency installation. MIT licenses are favorable for all three, but license metadata does not establish dependency, supply-chain, maintenance, or production-security clearance. Smallest reversible prototypes, if capacity later clears: transform one owned source document into draft SEO content and compare editorial acceptance; render one existing content flow with an isolated accessible component; add one static explanatory diagram to a high-intent page. Metrics would be draft acceptance/time-to-publish, task completion or CTA interaction, and organic impressions/clicks respectively. Time-to-learn is expected to be one isolated prototype cycle, but no implementation should start while capacity is saturated.
